ai.title: Add AgentOutput schema to SDK and backend
ai.summary: Introduced `AgentOutput` schema in `common/src/types/session-state.ts`, replacing ad-hoc result structures. `loopAgentSteps` and `mainPrompt` now return this typed output alongside `SessionState`, standardizing how agent results are propagated to the WebSocket layer. The `prompt-response` action in `common/src/actions.ts` accepts an optional `output` field, while `spawn-agents.ts` removes `formatAgentResult` in favor of direct output consumption. This unifies error and success handling across CLI, Web, and Desktop surfaces.

eli5.text: Starting today, agent results are delivered through a single, consistent format across the CLI, web, and desktop app instead of separate, ad-hoc formats per surface. Behind the scenes, the code that runs agent steps and spawns agents now returns a typed 'AgentOutput' containing either a last message or an error, which propagates up to the WebSocket layer that feeds your screen. You would notice this if you were watching the agent output path: sub-agents spawned via the spawn-agents handler and the mainPrompt entry point now return the same shape, and the prompt-response action accepts an optional output field to carry that payload. The old formatAgentResult helper has been removed in favor of directly consuming the typed output, so error and success cases are handled uniformly from this

ai.title: SDK 0.1.20 adds result.output, optional cwd, extraToolResults
ai.summary: Bumps @codebuff/sdk to 0.1.20. `result.output` now exposes agent output from awaited `client.run(...)` calls. `cwd` becomes optional in `CodebuffClient` constructor. `extraToolResults` parameter added to `run()` for additional context.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to do a task, you can now see what it actually produced in a dedicated output field, instead of only whether it succeeded. You can also start the assistant from a specific folder on your computer if you want, and give it extra notes to read while it works. These options are available now in the developer tools kit version released on September 1, 2025.

ai.title: codebuff 1.0.472 release
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.472 in `npm-app/release/package.json`. Routine internal release cycle. No functional changes or user-facing impact.

eli5.text: This release adds a small but important new way to read what the assistant produces: every response now comes with a clearly typed output that your tools can rely on, along with an optional working-folder setting and extra details from tool calls. It also adds a new agent configuration built on a newer model, and tightens up how the published SDK behaves so that cancelled inputs and skipped validations no longer surprise integrations. Behind the scenes, the team removed plaintext credentials from a setup guide, relicensed the SDK under Apache-2.0, and bumped internal concurrency and timeouts so overnight checks run more reliably. The change itself is just a version label bump to keep installs current.

ai.title: Unify max agent steps default to 25
ai.summary: MAX_AGENT_STEPS_DEFAULT set to 25 in common/src/constants/agents.ts, replacing divergent values 40 and 12. json-config/constants.ts and default.ts now import this constant, removing hardcoded literals. npm-app/src/client.ts refactors to reuse loaded config for stepsRemaining.

eli5.text: The assistant that works inside your project will now stop itself off after about 25 turns instead of stopping earlier at 12 or running longer at 40. If you watch a coding session, you may see it wrap up sooner than before when a task is taking a long time. This makes the timeout the same no matter how the assistant is started, so behavior is consistent between the local tool and the packaged app.

ai.title: init-agents command added
ai.summary: Added `init-agents` CLI command to `npm-app/src/index.ts`. Logic extracted from `agents.ts` into new `init-agents.ts` module. `createExampleAgentFiles` shared between `/agents` and `init-agents`. Refactors template import handling.

eli5.text: You can now run a single command to set up a starter kit of example projects in your local folder. That kit includes sample projects, a how-to guide, and the rules the system uses to recognize your project files, all pulled from the same shared library that the existing agents feature uses. The new setup command is live today and ready to use.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.473
ai.summary: Release version incremented to 1.0.473. Change applied to `npm-app/release/package.json`. Internal versioning update.

eli5.text: If you use CodeBuff today, updating to this release gives you an init-agents setup command for the assistant plus higher limits on how many reasoning steps agents can take before stopping. The version label itself just bumps the installed package number, which is a behind-the-scenes packaging step, not something you directly see.

ai.title: Unify maxAgentSteps constant in SDK and evals
ai.summary: SDK and eval runners now import MAX_AGENT_STEPS_DEFAULT from common/constants/agents. Replaces hardcoded 20 in codebuff.ts and DEFAULT_MAX_AGENT_STEPS in client.ts. Centralizes step limit logic across SDK and git-evals.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to solve a coding task, it does so in small steps and stops after a preset number to avoid running forever. That preset number used to live in two different places that could drift apart; now both point to a single shared definition. If you look at the system today, the limit is unchanged in practice, but it is now kept in one consistent spot so the SDK and the internal coding evaluations always agree.

ai.title: Tests reference MAXAGENTSTEPSDEFAULT constant
ai.summary: Test assertions in `common/src/json-config/__tests__/constants.test.ts` now import and use `MAX_AGENT_STEPS_DEFAULT` from `src/constants/agents` instead of hardcoded value `12`. This decouples test expectations from the literal default value, ensuring tests reflect the actual constant used by the config schema. Scope is limited to test files within the shared core package.

eli5.text: When the default cap on how many steps an automated helper can take changes, the safety checks that watch this limit used to look for a specific written-in number. Now they look at the same named setting the rest of the software uses, so if someone changes the default value later, the checks will follow automatically instead of being left behind. If you looked, you'd see the test expectations referencing that shared name instead of a plain number. This is a behind-the-scenes code-health fix with no visible change to how anything works.
